title: MCP in practice — the trading floor
intro: Week 6 spends the protocol: equip agents from servers, then let four traders loose.

steps.title: Three moves inside the SDK
steps.body: 1. **Create a client**, 2. **have it spawn the server**, 3. **collect the tools** — then hand them to an `Agent` like any other tools. The first lab does it with the fetch server from the MCP course; the same three moves work for every server after.

points.label: All-local
points.note: The knowledge-graph memory server: persistent entities, observations, relationships — your agent remembers across sessions.

points.label: Local + web
points.note: Runs locally, calls a service: Brave Search, financial data. A thin authenticated bridge.

points.label: Remote
points.note: Fully remote services — the MCP pack's territory; here they're a consumer's choice.

steps.title: Autonomous Traders
steps.body:
The capstone: **four trader agents + a researcher**, each equipped with the home-made **Accounts MCP server** (balance/holdings/buy/sell **tools**, plus **resources**: `accounts://…` account state and an investment-strategy resource), fetch, memory, search, and market data.

Traders read their strategy *as a resource*, research *via tools*, and act — autonomously, on a loop.

steps.title: What the capstone asserts
steps.body:
The money logic lives in a **server**, not in any agent — so one accounts server serves four different traders, and swapping a trader's brain never touches the accounting. State is **resources**; actions are **tools**; instructions are a **versioned resource**, not vibes.

> [!warn] Four autonomous agents with buy/sell tools is the course's most honest risk demo: this is where budgets, termination caps, and guardrails stop being theory.

recap:
**Equip agents from servers; keep state, actions and instructions separated.**

- Client → spawn server → collect tools → hand to Agent.
- Server shapes: all-local (memory), local+web (search/data), remote.
- Accounts server: tools for actions, resources for state and strategy.
- Autonomy at capstone scale = budgets and guardrails, mandatory.
